theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Your supervisor gives you a list of jobs for the day. What should you do first?
options: Start on the job you like best, so that the day goes well
Do the quickest jobs first and leave the hard ones for later
Read the list, check you understand it and ask about anything unclear
Share out the jobs to the other trainees and then wait for a client

questions.stem: In planning, what is a 'priority'?
options: A job that you can leave until the end of the week
A job that only the salon owner is allowed to do
A job that is more important or urgent than others
A job that is paid for in cash before it is started

questions.stem: It is 8:30 a.m. on a busy Saturday. Which job should a salon assistant do first?
options: Re-arrange the product shelves in colour order for the display
Count the shampoo in the store room for next month's order
Clean the front windows of the salon to give a fresh look
Set up the basins and stations for the 9:00 a.m. clients

questions.stem: Which of these is a SMART goal for a trainee?
options: Get much better at doing all kinds of hair at some time this year
Be the best and most famous stylist in the whole of Jamaica
Do five roller sets to the assessor's standard by 30 November
Try to work a little bit faster with my clients in future

questions.stem: Why does a salon keep an appointment book or booking app?
options: To plan each stylist's time and avoid booking two clients at once
To keep a list of all the clients who still owe the salon some money
To record the stock that has been used up during each day
To show the tax office how many hours the cleaner has worked

questions.stem: A blow-dry takes about 45 minutes, and the stylist needs 15 minutes to clean and reset the station after it. A client is booked at 10:00 a.m. What is the earliest time for the stylist's next client?
What is a 'buffer' in an appointment plan?
options: A client who is booked in without telling the stylist
A short spare time left between bookings for delays
A list of clients who are waiting for a cancellation
The extra cost added when a client comes in late

questions.stem: Shanice, the receptionist, books a relaxer and a full set of box braids with the same stylist at the same time. What is this mistake called?
options: Double booking
Over-charging
Walk-in booking
Block booking

questions.stem: Before a busy weekend, why should you check the stock of shampoo, conditioner and other products?
options: So that you can take home anything that is close to its expiry date
So that you can move all the stock into the salon's front window
So that you can change the products to cheaper ones each week
So that you can order what is low before it runs out on the day

questions.stem: What does 'first in, first out' (FIFO) mean for salon stock?
options: The first client who arrives is the first one to be served
The newest stock is used first because it is the freshest
The stylist who comes in first is the first to go home
The oldest stock is used before the newer stock is opened

questions.stem: What is a 're-order level' for a salon product?
options: The highest number of items the store room can hold
The price at which the salon sells each product to clients
The amount left in stock at which you order more
The number of items damaged in the last delivery

questions.stem: What is the best way to plan the tools and products for a client's service?
options: Collect each item when you find you need it during the service
Borrow from the next station so that you do not have to walk
List what the service needs and set it out before the client sits
Ask the client to bring their own tools and products from home

questions.stem: Why should a stylist know roughly how long each service takes?
options: So that they can charge the client extra each time a service runs over
So that bookings can be planned and clients are not kept waiting
So that they can leave early whenever a service is quick
So that they can do two services at once for each client

questions.topic: Dealing with changes to the plan
questions.stem: A client arrives 25 minutes late for a 45-minute blow-dry, and the next client is booked straight after. What should the stylist do?
options: Do the full service anyway and let the next client wait as long as it takes
Turn the client away in front of everyone and tell her not to come back
Follow the salon's policy: offer a shorter service, or a new time
Rush the blow-dry with the dryer on its highest heat to catch up

questions.stem: The phone rings while you are sweeping hair from your station, and no one else is free. What should you do?
options: Let it ring, because the sweeping must be finished first
Leave the broom across the walkway and run to the phone
Ask the client in the chair to answer the phone for you
Put the broom safely aside and answer the phone politely

questions.stem: What is a 'work plan'?
options: A list of the salon's prices that is shown to the clients
A list of the tasks to do, in order, with times and resources
A drawing of the salon that shows where the fire exits are
A record of how many hours each worker has been paid for

questions.stem: Why is it useful to break a big job, such as a deep clean of the whole salon, into smaller steps?
options: Each step is easier to plan, share out and check when done
It means the job can be left unfinished without a problem
It allows the job to be done without telling the supervisor
It makes the job need more people and take more time

questions.stem: Your supervisor asks you to finish setting up the colour bar, but you have not been trained to mix tints. What should you do?
options: Mix the tints anyway, following the picture on the box
Tell the supervisor you are not trained and ask for help
Leave the job without saying anything and do something else
Ask a client who colours her own hair to show you how

questions.stem: Which of these is the most efficient layout for a styling station?
options: Tools kept in the store room and fetched one at a time
Products for all services piled together on the counter
Electrical tools left plugged in on the floor by the chair
Tools and products in reach, cables tidy and the floor clear

questions.stem: Why should you tidy and reset your work area after each client, and not only at the end of the day?
options: So that the supervisor can see how busy you have been all day
So that the next client starts on time in a clean, safe area
So that you can use up more of the cleaning products each week
So that the client feels they must leave the salon quickly

questions.stem: What does 'teamwork' mean in a salon?
options: Each person does only their own work and does not help others
The most senior stylist does all the clients while others watch
Staff share tasks and help each other to give a good service
Everyone works on the same client at the same time

questions.stem: You must leave the floor for a short time while your client is under the hood dryer. What should you do first?
options: Hand over to a colleague, telling them the time and what is next
Turn the dryer up high so the hair is dry when you come back
Tell the client to call you on your phone when she feels ready
Leave and come back later, as the dryer has its own timer

questions.stem: What is the main reason for writing your tasks on a list?
options: So that nothing is forgotten and jobs can be ticked off when done
So that the supervisor has a paper to sign at the end of the day
So that you have something to show clients who ask about you
So that the list can be thrown away when the first job is done

questions.stem: Easter, Christmas and graduation are busy times for salons in Jamaica. How should the salon plan for them?
options: Close the salon for a few days so that the staff can rest
Plan staff, bookings and stock early, before the rush starts
Take only walk-in clients, so that there is no booking to do
Give each client a shorter service with no consultation at all

questions.topic: Dealing with changes to the plan
questions.stem: On a Friday afternoon the electricity goes off in the salon. What should you do first?
options: Leave all the dryers and irons switched on so they restart when the power comes back
Send every client home straight away without telling the supervisor
Make the clients safe, switch off and unplug tools, and tell the supervisor
Light candles at each station so the stylists can carry on working

questions.topic: Dealing with changes to the plan
questions.stem: The water supply to the area will be off for the whole day. Which plan is the most sensible?
options: Carry on with shampoos, using bottled drinking water from the shop
Book in more chemical services, as they need less rinsing time
Do every client's shampoo with dry shampoo instead of water
Tell the supervisor, call clients and move services that need water

questions.topic: Dealing with changes to the plan
questions.stem: A stylist calls in sick and has six clients booked. What should the receptionist do first?
options: Wait and see which of the clients turn up, then tell them at the door
Tell the supervisor, then contact clients to rebook or move them
Cancel every booking for the day without telling the clients

questions.stem: You can see that you will not finish a task by the time your supervisor set. What should you do?
options: Say nothing and hope that the supervisor does not notice
Tell the supervisor early and agree what to do next
Hand the task to a client who is waiting in reception
Rush the work and skip the safety checks to save time

questions.stem: Why is it important to follow the salon's policies and procedures when you plan your work?
options: They let each stylist do things in their own different way each day
They make sure work is planned only by the salon owner
They keep the service safe, legal and the same for every client
They mean you never need to ask the supervisor anything

questions.stem: Which of these is a 'resource' when planning salon work?
options: Staff time, tools, products and equipment
The weather forecast for the next week
The colour of the walls in the waiting area
The radio station playing in the salon

questions.stem: Tashana is getting ready for a roller set. In what order should she work?
options: Start the client, then look for the rollers, then read the booking
Read the booking, start the client, then fetch products as they are needed
Fetch the products, start the client, then read the booking
Read the booking, collect and check the tools, then start the client

questions.stem: Why should you check that equipment such as hood dryers and steamers works before the clients arrive?
options: So that you can use the time to charge your own phone
So that you can tell each client about the faults as they arrive
So that you can switch it on and leave it running all day
So that faults are found and reported before they hold up work

questions.stem: Andre has finished all his tasks an hour early. What is the best thing for him to do?
options: Go home early without telling anyone, as his work is done
Tell the supervisor and offer to help with other tasks
Sit in the waiting area and chat with clients on his phone
Start doing his finished tasks again so that he looks busy

questions.stem: What is the best way to check that you are keeping to your plan during the day?
options: Wait until closing time and then look back at the whole day
Ask each client at the end of the service if they were on time
Check your list and the clock at set times and adjust if needed
Keep working as fast as you can and never look at the plan

questions.stem: Why should a salon keep a record of work that went wrong or ran late?
options: So that the cause can be found and the plan improved next time
So that the worker can be blamed in front of the rest of the team
So that clients can be charged extra for the time lost
So that the salon has more paper files to keep in storage

questions.stem: Which question is the most useful when you review how your day went?
options: Which of today's clients gave me the biggest tips?
What went well, and what could I do better next time?
How early can I leave work tomorrow afternoon?
Which of the other trainees was the slowest worker today?

questions.stem: What is 'feedback' from a supervisor?
options: A list of the jobs that you must do on your next shift
A written warning that is kept in your personal file
A note of the clients who asked for you by name
Comments on how well you did and how you can improve

questions.stem: A client asks a trainee for a service the trainee is not yet allowed to do, such as a relaxer. What should the trainee do?
options: Explain politely and pass the client to a qualified stylist
Do the relaxer quickly before the supervisor comes back from lunch
Tell the client that relaxers are bad and refuse to talk
Book the relaxer in for herself on her day off at home

questions.stem: Why should you plan time to clean and disinfect tools between clients?
options: So that there are always clean tools ready and germs are not spread
So that each client waits a while and feels they got good value
So that the stylist can take a short rest after each client
So that the salon can charge an extra cleaning fee to each client

questions.stem: You have a client in your chair, a delivery driver waiting at the door and towels to fold. Which comes first?
options: Fold the towels, as the job is quick and easy
Carry on caring for the client in the chair
Check the delivery, as the driver is waiting
Stop and ask another client which job to do

questions.stem: What is the main reason for using a daily checklist to open the salon?
options: So that only the owner knows how to open the salon
So that every opening job is done the same way each day
So that the salon can open later than its stated time
So that staff do not need to arrive on time each day

questions.stem: Which is an example of good time management for a trainee?
options: Taking long phone calls between clients to stay relaxed
Starting each job before finding out what it needs
Arriving early to set up and prepare for the first client
Leaving all the cleaning up until the very last minute of the day

questions.stem: Why should you tell the receptionist when a service is running late?
options: So she can tell the client in the chair to hurry up
So she can give the next client a lower price
So she can stop answering the telephone for the rest of the day
So she can warn the next client and adjust the bookings

questions.stem: What does it mean to 'delegate' a task?
options: To give a task to another suitable person to do
To put a task off until another day of the week
To refuse a task because it is not in your job
To do a task again because it was done badly

questions.stem: At closing time, which job helps the next day start smoothly?
options: Restock the stations and leave a note of anything low or faulty
Leave the used towels in a pile on the basins for the morning
Switch off the lights while the last client is still drying
Take the appointment book home so that no one else can see it

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In a SMART goal, what does the letter 'S' stand for?
A full set of box braids takes 6 hours. The stylist starts at 8:00 a.m. and takes no breaks. At what time will she finish?
What do we call a client who comes into the salon without an appointment?
What is it called when you count all the products in the salon and store room to check the stock records?
There are 12 bottles of conditioner in stock and 7 are used this week. How many bottles are left?
A relaxer service takes 1 hour 30 minutes. How many minutes is that?
What word do we use for the salon's written rules on how things must be done?
Which person should a trainee report to first about a problem with their work in the salon?
What do we call the times when the salon is busiest, such as Saturdays and the weeks before Christmas?
Four clients each book a 45-minute service with the same stylist. How many hours of work is that?
What one word describes a task that must be done straight away?
A box of 10 neck strips costs J$600. How much does one neck strip cost?
What is the name of the card or sheet that records each product coming into and going out of stock?
A stylist works from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and takes 1 hour for lunch. How many hours does she work?
What word means making the best use of time, materials and effort, without waste?

essays.stem: Explain the steps you would follow to plan and organise your own work for a day in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: First I find out what the day needs. I read the appointment book and any jobs the supervisor has given me, and I ask about anything I do not understand. Next I list all my tasks, such as the clients I will assist, setting up the basins, cleaning and restocking. I put them in order of priority, with the most urgent and important first, and give each one a time. Then I plan the resources: the tools, products, towels and equipment for each service. I check that equipment works and that stock is enough, and report anything low or faulty. During the day I check my list and the clock at set times, tell the supervisor early if I am falling behind, and change the plan if something goes wrong. At the end of the day I tick off what is done, tidy and restock, and think about what I could do better.
markingPoints: Finds out the day's work from the bookings and the supervisor, and asks about anything unclear
Lists the tasks and puts them in order of priority, with times
Plans and checks the resources: tools, products, equipment and stock
Checks progress during the day and reports or adjusts the plan when needed
Reviews the work at the end of the day and leaves the area ready

essays.stem: Describe how you would decide which tasks to do first. Use an example from a busy Saturday in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: I sort tasks by how urgent and how important they are. Urgent tasks must be done now; important tasks affect clients, safety or the salon's work. Tasks that are both come first. Safety comes before everything: a wet floor or a faulty dryer must be dealt with at once. Clients in the chair come next, because they are paying for our time. Tasks that are important but not urgent, such as stock counting, are planned for a quiet time. For example, on a busy Saturday at 8:30 a.m. I would set up the basins and stations for the 9:00 a.m. clients first, check the dryers work, and put out clean towels. Folding spare towels or tidying the product display can wait until after the morning rush. If I am not sure what comes first, I ask the supervisor.
markingPoints: Explains urgent and important, and that tasks which are both come first
Puts safety first
Puts clients being served ahead of other tasks
Gives a sensible example from a busy Saturday, in the right order
Leaves less urgent tasks for quiet times, and asks the supervisor if unsure

essays.stem: Explain how a well-kept appointment book helps the salon run smoothly, and say what should be written down for each booking.
essays.modelAnswer: A well-kept appointment book, on paper or in an app, shows each stylist's day at a glance. It stops double booking, because each time slot is filled only once. It lets the salon plan staff, tools and products, so that the right things are ready for each client. It helps the receptionist give clients a real time and tell them if there is a delay. It shows quiet times, when cleaning or stock checks can be done, and busy times when more staff are needed. For each booking the receptionist should write the client's name and phone number, the service and how long it takes, the stylist, the date and time, and any notes such as a skin test needed before a chemical service. A small buffer between bookings allows for delays. Bookings should be written clearly so that anyone can read them.
markingPoints: Stops double booking and shows each stylist's time
Helps plan staff, tools and products for each service
Lets the salon keep clients informed and use quiet times well
Records name, phone number, service, length, stylist, date and time, plus notes
Mentions buffer time or writing clearly

essays.stem: Describe how you would check and keep the salon's stock so that products do not run out or go out of date.
essays.modelAnswer: I would count the stock on a set day each week, for example every Monday morning before clients arrive, and write the numbers on the stock card or sheet. I would compare each count with the re-order level. Anything at or below that level goes on the order list for the supervisor. Before a busy time such as Christmas or graduation, I would order more in good time. When new stock arrives I would check it against the delivery note for the right items, number and condition. I would put new stock behind the old stock, so that the oldest is used first, and check expiry dates. Products are stored as the maker says: cool, dry and out of the sun, with chemicals kept separate and closed. I would report any damaged, leaking or out-of-date products and record them.
markingPoints: Counts stock regularly and records it on a stock card or sheet
Compares with the re-order level and orders in good time, especially before busy periods
Checks deliveries against the delivery note
Uses the oldest stock first and checks expiry dates
Stores products as the maker says and reports damaged or out-of-date items

essays.stem: Explain why teamwork and clear communication are important when planning salon work. Give two examples.
essays.modelAnswer: A salon works as a team. The receptionist, stylists and assistants depend on one another, so a plan only works if everyone knows it and does their part. Clear communication means saying what you will do, asking when you are not sure, and telling others early when something changes. Teamwork means sharing tasks and helping when someone is busy. For example, if a colour service is running late, the stylist tells the receptionist, who can warn the next client and move the bookings, while an assistant starts the next client's shampoo. Another example is a handover: if a stylist must leave the floor while a client is under the dryer, she tells a colleague the time left and what comes next, so the client is not forgotten. Good teamwork keeps clients happy, saves time and makes the salon a better place to work.
markingPoints: Explains that staff depend on one another, so everyone must know the plan
Says what clear communication means: tell, ask, and report changes early
Says what teamwork means: share tasks and help when someone is busy
Gives two sensible salon examples
Links teamwork to happy clients, saved time or a better workplace

essays.stem: Explain what a SMART goal is. Write one SMART goal for your own training and show how it meets each letter.
essays.modelAnswer: A SMART goal is a clear target that you can plan for and check. S is specific: it says exactly what you will do. M is measurable: you can count or check it. A is achievable: you can really do it with the time and help you have. R is relevant: it matters to your training or job. T is time-bound: it has a date to finish by. My goal is: 'I will complete five roller sets on training heads to my assessor's standard by 30 November.' It is specific because it names roller sets. It is measurable because I can count five and the assessor can check the standard. It is achievable because I have two practical sessions a week. It is relevant because roller setting is part of my course. It is time-bound because it ends on 30 November. I would tick off each set as I finish it.
markingPoints: Explains that a SMART goal is clear and can be checked
Gives the meaning of all five letters correctly
Writes a sensible goal about their own training
Shows how the goal meets each letter
Says how progress towards the goal will be checked

essays.stem: Describe how you would set out your station before a shampoo and blow-dry so that you can work efficiently and safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the client arrives I check the booking so I know the service and the hair type. At the basin I put out clean towels, a gown and cape, and the shampoo and conditioner for that hair type, and I check that the water runs at a comfortable temperature. At the styling station I wipe the chair, counter and mirror with disinfectant. I set out clean, disinfected combs and brushes, sectioning clips, heat protectant and finishing products, all within easy reach. I check the blow-dryer: the plug, cable and filter. I plug it in near the station and keep the cable off the floor where people walk. I check that the floor is dry and free of hair, and that the hand mirror and bin are in place. Having everything ready means I do not leave the client to look for things, the service runs to time, and the area stays safe.
markingPoints: Checks the booking to know the service and hair type
Prepares the basin: towels, gown, products, water temperature
Cleans the station and sets out disinfected tools and products within reach
Checks the dryer and keeps cables safe and the floor dry and clear
Explains that this saves time and keeps the service safe

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep track of your progress during the working day, and what you would do if you started to fall behind.
essays.modelAnswer: I keep my task list where I can see it and check it, with the clock, at set times such as every hour and after each client. I tick off each task when it is done, so I can see what is left. I compare the time each service is really taking with the time booked. If I start to fall behind, I tell the supervisor and the receptionist early, not at the last minute. Together we decide what to do: the receptionist can warn the next client, a colleague may help with a shampoo or clean-up, or a task that is not urgent can be moved to later. I do not rush in a way that is unsafe, skip hygiene steps or lower the quality of the work. At the end of the day I note why I fell behind, so that I can plan better next time.
markingPoints: Checks the task list and the clock at set times and ticks off tasks
Compares real service times with booked times
Tells the supervisor and receptionist early if falling behind
Agrees a change: help from a colleague, warn clients, or move non-urgent tasks
Does not cut corners on safety, hygiene or quality, and notes the cause for next time

essays.stem: Explain how you would review your work at the end of a day or week, and how you would use feedback to improve.
essays.modelAnswer: At the end of the day I look back at my plan. I check which tasks were done, which were late or left out, and why. I ask myself what went well and what I could do better. I look at whether my timings were right and whether I had the tools and products I needed. I also listen to feedback from my supervisor, instructor, workmates and clients. I accept it politely, without arguing, and ask questions if I do not understand. I write down one or two points to work on, for example being quicker at sectioning, or setting up before the client arrives. I make those points part of my plan for the next day or week, and then check later whether I have improved. Reviewing like this helps me become faster, safer and more skilled.
markingPoints: Compares what was done with the plan and finds the reasons for problems
Asks what went well and what could be better, including timings and resources
Listens to feedback politely and asks questions
Writes down points to improve and puts them into the next plan
Checks later whether there has been improvement

essays.stem: Describe the jobs that should be on a salon's opening and closing checklists, and explain how these checklists help the work run smoothly.
essays.modelAnswer: An opening checklist might include: unlock and switch on lights and fans; check the floor, basins and stations are clean and dry; check equipment such as dryers, steamers and irons works and cables are safe; put out clean towels and gowns; restock products at each station; check the appointment book for the day; and check the first-aid box. A closing checklist might include: clean and disinfect all tools; wipe down basins, chairs and counters; sweep and mop the floor; put used towels in the laundry; switch off and unplug equipment; store chemicals safely and close all containers; empty bins; note anything low or faulty for the supervisor; and lock up. Checklists make sure nothing is forgotten, even on a busy or tiring day. Every person does the jobs the same way, so the salon is safe, clean and ready on time.
markingPoints: Lists sensible opening jobs, including checking equipment and the day's bookings
Lists sensible closing jobs, including cleaning, unplugging and storing chemicals
Includes noting low stock or faults for the supervisor
Explains that checklists stop jobs being forgotten
Explains that everyone works the same way, so the salon is safe and ready on time

practical1.title: Plan a salon Saturday: appointment schedule and work plan
practical1.brief: Your group is the planning team for a salon with three stylists and one assistant, open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on a Saturday. The assessor gives you a list of client requests: the service each client wants, how long it takes, and any times they cannot come. As a group: (1) draw up a timetable for the day on chart paper or the Centre's booking sheet, with each stylist's clients, a short buffer between bookings, cleaning time and a lunch break for every staff member; (2) write a work plan for the assistant, with the opening jobs, the jobs during the day and the closing jobs, in order and with times; (3) list the tools and products needed for each type of service. Share the work so that each member plans one stylist's or the assistant's day, then check each other's plans for clashes. Each member then explains their part to the assessor. Photograph each stage. Hand in once for the whole group with the photos and the finished sheets.
materials: The client request list given by the assessor
Blank booking sheets or chart paper with a time grid (every 15 minutes)
Rulers, pencils, erasers and coloured markers
The Centre's service list with the usual time for each service
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: The client request list with the group's first notes
The draft timetable, before checking for clashes
The finished timetable, with buffers, cleaning time and lunch breaks marked
The list of tools and products for each service
Each member pointing to their part of the plan while explaining it (sheets and hands only, no faces)
checklist: Read the client requests and took part in sharing out the work
Booked each client in a suitable time slot, with no double booking
Allowed a realistic time for each service, with a buffer and cleaning time
Gave every staff member a lunch break and kept within opening hours
Wrote opening, daytime and closing jobs in a sensible order with times
Listed the right tools and products for the services planned
Checked another member's plan and helped fix any clash
Explained their own part of the plan clearly to the assessor
safety: Plan breaks: tired staff make mistakes with heat and chemicals
Leave time to clean and disinfect tools between clients
Do not plan more work than the staff can do safely in the time
Keep the work area tidy, with bags and chairs out of walkways

practical2.title: Stock check, re-order list and a salon opening and closing checklist poster
practical2.brief: As a group, carry out a stock check in the Centre's training salon. Each member counts one area (for example the basins, the styling stations, the store room shelf and the laundry and towels) and writes the count, the expiry dates they find and any damaged items on a stock sheet. Together, compare each count with the re-order level the assessor gives, and write a re-order list with quantities and costs in J$ from the Centre's price list. Do not add any tax unless the assessor gives you a figure. Then make an A3 poster with the salon's opening checklist on one side and its closing checklist on the other, to be put up in the salon. Each member writes at least two of the checklist jobs and explains one to the assessor. Photograph each stage. Hand in once for the whole group with the photos, the stock sheets, the re-order list and the poster.
materials: Blank stock sheets with columns for item, count, expiry date, condition and re-order level
The re-order levels and the Centre's price list, from the assessor
A3 card or chart paper and coloured markers
Disposable gloves for handling chemical containers
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: Each member counting their area, with the stock sheet in view
The completed stock sheets, side by side
The re-order list with quantities and J$ costs
The finished opening and closing checklist poster
The store room shelves left tidy, with the oldest stock at the front
